title: Categorical contractibility of the finite inverse gadget
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, coherent functor categories and coherent functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes enlarged as necessary. Let $Q$ be the degreewise pushout $$Q=\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}\amalg\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}(\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0),$$ where the edge with vertices $0,2$ is collapsed to the first point and the edge with vertices $1,3$ to the second point. For every quasicategory $E$, restriction along the unique map $p:Q\to\Delta^0$ gives a coherent functor equivalence $$p^*:E=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E).$$ No quasicategory or Kan condition is imposed on $Q$, and $E$ may be empty.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.2.7 (05ZJ): Q to the point is a categorical equivalence, in the whole-functor-category formulation of categorical equivalence. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this higher categorical assertion. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix any quasicategory $E$. Let $H_1(E)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ on equivalence edges. The constant-arrow map $k:E\to H_1(E)$ and evaluation $v$ at vertex $0$ satisfy $vk=1$. The monotone function $m:[1]\times[1]\to[1]$, $m(i,t)=\min(i,t)$, induces a transformation $kv\to1_{H_1(E)}$: for each parameter simplex $A:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to E$, use $A(m(i,t),z)$, keeping $z\in\Delta^n$ unchanged. This formula commutes with all simplicial operators. At an object $f:x\to y$ its two vertex components are $1_x,f$, both equivalences. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] its component in the arrow category is an equivalence. Fullness retains its inverse and inverse-triangle simplices inside $H_1(E)$. Apply the same pointwise criterion with shape $H_1(E)$ and target $H_1(E)$ to conclude that the whole transformation is an equivalence. All these functor simplicial sets and full subcategories are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus $k$ is a coherent equivalence, and $\Delta^1\to\Delta^0$ localizes at the nondegenerate edge, in the sense of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map].

source.place: 05ZJ first sentence, expanding 05ZG through Example 6.3.1.14: interval collapse.

proof.text: Put $A=\Delta^{\{0,2\}}\amalg\Delta^{\{1,3\}}$, $B=\Delta^0\amalg\Delta^0$, and let $c:A\to B$ collapse the two components separately. Let $V$ be the two nondegenerate edges of $A$. Degreewise $\operatorname{Fun}(A,E)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)^2$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)=E^2$, since product with $\Delta^n$ distributes over the two-component coproduct. The $V$-inverting full subcategory is $H_1(E)^2$. The product of the two copies of $v$ in step 1 is a quasi-inverse to $c^*$, and its two inverse equivalences and their triangle witnesses are the coordinatewise pairs of those in step 1. Thus $c$ localizes at $V$. The inclusion $i:A\to\Delta^3$ is injective in each degree: its images are the increasing vertex strings taking values in $\{0,2\}$ or $\{1,3\}$; these sets of strings are disjoint.

source.place: 05ZG monomorphism hypothesis and its coproduct-of-intervals localization input; verified directly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-localization-monomorphic-pushout] to the source span $(X_{01},X_0,X_1)=(A,\Delta^3,A)$ with legs $(i,1_A)$, and the target span $(Y_{01},Y_0,Y_1)=(A,\Delta^3,B)$ with legs $(i,c)$. The vertical maps are $(p_{01},p_0,p_1)=(1_A,1_{\Delta^3},c)$. Both zeroth legs are the degreewise injection $i$ from step 2. Set $V_{01}=V_0=\varnothing$, $V_1=V$. The identity vertical maps localize at the empty collection, and $c$ localizes at $V$ by step 2; both required edge-image inclusions are vacuous. The source pushout is $\Delta^3$ and the target pushout is the specified $Q$. Therefore the quotient $a:\Delta^3\to Q$ localizes at the edges $W=\{02,13\}$. In particular for every $E$ its restriction factors as a coherent equivalence $r:\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)\to L_W(E)$, where $L_W(E)$ is the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^3,E)$ on diagrams inverting $02,13$.

source.place: 05ZJ first sentence / 05ZG: explicit map of monomorphic pushout spans.

proof.text: We identify $L_W(E)$ with the full subcategory $L_{\rm all}(E)$ of diagrams inverting every edge of $\Delta^3$. Let $F:\Delta^3\to E$, write $f=F(01)$, $g=F(12)$, $h=F(23)$, and suppose $F(02),F(13)$ are equivalences. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], the faces give $[g][f]=[F(02)]$ and $[h][g]=[F(13)]$ in $hE$. Put $u=([g][f])^{-1}$ and $w=([h][g])^{-1}$. Then $[f]u$ is a right inverse to $[g]$, and $w[h]$ is a left inverse. They coincide because $w[h]=w[h][g]([f]u)=[f]u$. Hence $[g]$ is invertible. Now $[f]=[g]^{-1}[F(02)]$ and $[h]=[F(13)][g]^{-1}$ are invertible, as is $[F(03)]=[h][g][f]$. The cited node identifies invertible classes precisely with equivalence edges. This lists all six nondegenerate edges; degenerate edges are identities. The converse is immediate. Thus the two full subcategories have exactly the same vertices, and hence the same simplices by the full-subcategory definition.

Let $q:\Delta^3\to\Delta^0$. The constant-diagram map $t:E\to L_{\rm all}(E)$ is a coherent equivalence with quasi-inverse evaluation $v_0$ at vertex $0$. Indeed $v_0t=1_E$. The monotone function $b:[3]\times[1]\to[3]$ given by $b(i,0)=0$ and $b(i,1)=i$ defines a transformation $tv_0\to1$: on a parameter simplex $F:\Delta^3\times\Delta^n\to E$ use $F(b(i,s),z)$. At its two endpoints this is respectively the constant diagram on $F(0,z)$ and $F(i,z)$, so fullness makes this a transformation in $L_{\rm all}(E)$. At an object $F$ its component is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^3,E)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences], since its components are the edges $F(0i)$, all equivalences. Its inverse witnesses stay in the full subcategory. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] that subcategory is a quasicategory. Applying the pointwise criterion once more with shape and target $L_{\rm all}(E)$ makes the entire transformation a coherent natural equivalence. This proves directly the assertion in 05ZJ that $q$ localizes at all edges, and step 4 identifies its image with $L_W(E)$.

source.place: 05ZJ middle sentences: the projection of the simplex localizes at all its edges; explicit constant-diagram contraction retaining all transformations.

proof.text: We finish with the specified precomposition map, retaining higher simplices. Since $q=pa$, the functors from steps 3 and 5 satisfy $r p^*=t$ strictly, with common target $L_W(E)=L_{\rm all}(E)$. A coherent functor equivalence induces an ordinary equivalence on homotopy categories: apply its quasi-inverse, and take the component classes of its coherent inverse transformations; each naturality square gives the naturality equation by its two triangle relations in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Thus $h(r)$ and $h(t)$ are equivalences. Ordinary cancellation gives that $h(p^*)$ is an equivalence: if $R$ is a quasi-inverse to $h(r)$, then $h(p^*)\cong R h(r)h(p^*)=R h(t)$, a composite of equivalences. This holds for every quasicategory $E$ in every sufficiently large universe. Apply (iii)$\Rightarrow$(ii) of [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test] to the simplicial map $p:Q\to\Delta^0$. It gives exactly that $p^*:E\to\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)$ is a coherent functor equivalence. The test allows arbitrary simplicial source and target, so no quasicategory condition on $Q$ was used. If $E$ is empty, both $\operatorname{Fun}(Q,E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^3,E)$ are empty since these shapes have vertices; all preceding equivalences and contractions are then the unique maps of empty simplicial sets.
